For anyone who's interested, in printing, there are four component ("process") inks that are used to print full-color pieces: cyan (blue), magenta (red), yellow, and black. Inks are translucent, including black. Trying to cover a large, solid area with black ink is problematic; the ink doesn't soak into the paper smoothly, and the result looks mottled. The solution is to add at least one of the other process inks to the black area; this increases the depth or "richness" of the black.

This preference in Illustrator and InDesign simply determines how black colors are displayed on screen: "accurately" means that elements colored with only black ink will look "lighter" than elements with process colors mixed into the black.
